meta.name: Europe
meta.description: All European STEM & Physics research hubs, universities, deep-tech startups, and regional historical milestones for offline exploration.

eras.label: Pre-Classical & Ancient Foundations
eras.summary: Quantitative astronomy, metrology, optics, statics, hydrostatics, and naturalistic cosmology across Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and the Mediterranean.

eras.label: Golden Ages & Medieval Optics
eras.summary: Experimental optics, magnetism, algebra of motion, and precision observatories across the Islamic Golden Age, Song China, India, and medieval Europe.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution
eras.summary: Heliocentrism, telescopic astronomy, laws of planetary motion, universal gravitation, calculus, and analytical mechanics.

eras.label: Electromagnetism & Thermodynamics
eras.summary: Unification of electricity, magnetism, and light; statistical entropy; X-rays; and the discovery of radioactivity.

eras.label: Relativity & Quantum Century
eras.summary: Spacetime curvature, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, QED, semiconductor electronics, cosmic microwave background, and the Standard Model.

eras.label: Precision & Mega-Experiments
eras.summary: High-Tc superconductors, Bose-Einstein condensates, neutrino mass, dark energy, graphene, Higgs boson, gravitational waves, black hole imaging, and fusion ignition.

eras.label: Upcoming Frontier (2027–2045+)
eras.summary: Next-generation compact and burning-plasma fusion, 39 m optical telescopes, gigaton neutrino observatories, space interferometers, and post-LHC colliders.

spaceZones.label: Earth & LEO
spaceZones.desc: Orbital physics labs, telescopes, and particle detectors around Earth

spaceZones.label: The Moon
spaceZones.desc: Lunar laser ranging, seismology, and far-side radio astrophysics (~1.28 light-sec)

spaceZones.label: Sun & Inner Planets
spaceZones.desc: Heliophysics, Mercury, Venus, and inner solar system probes

spaceZones.label: Mars & Asteroids
spaceZones.desc: Martian seismology, atmosphere physics, and asteroid sample returns (~12.5 light-min)

spaceZones.label: Gas & Ice Giants
spaceZones.desc: Jupiter, Saturn, magnetospheres, icy moons, and outer-planet physics

spaceZones.label: Kuiper Belt to ~1 Light-Day
spaceZones.desc: New Horizons, heliopause, and Voyager 1 & 2 reaching ~1 light-day from Earth

hubs.name: CERN
hubs.summary: Home of the 27 km Large Hadron Collider, smashing protons at 99.999999% the speed of light to probe the building blocks of matter.
hubs.nobel: Confirmed the Higgs boson (2012) and W/Z bosons (Rubbia & van der Meer, 1984).

hubs.name: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research (PIK)
hubs.summary: Occupying Potsdam's historic Telegrafenberg science hill beside the Einstein Tower—global pioneer of Earth-system tipping points, Planetary Boundaries (Johan Rockström), integrated energy-economy models (REMIND), and complex-network climate physics.
hubs.nobel: Shaped the 1.5°C/2°C Paris Agreement scientific guardrail and the Planetary Boundaries framework guiding global sustainability.

stages.highschool: Explore PIK's interactive Planetary Health Check and Climate Tipping Points explainers.

events.title: Aristarchus of Samos: Heliocentric Model & Cosmic Distances
events.summary: Proposed a heliocentric model placing the Sun at the center with Earth rotating daily and orbiting annually, and used lunar-phase geometry to estimate relative Sun-Moon sizes and distances.
events.impact: Demonstrated trigonometric cosmic distance measurement and anticipated Copernican heliocentrism by 1,800 years.

events.title: Archimedes' Principle, Statics & Law of the Lever
events.summary: Formulated exact mathematical laws of buoyancy (On Floating Bodies), centers of gravity, levers, and early exhaustion methods anticipating integral calculus.
events.impact: Established mathematical physics as a rigorous deductive discipline bridging geometry and mechanics.

events.title: Robert Grosseteste's De Luce & Mathematical Optics
events.summary: Argued that physical nature must be understood through geometry and light (De Luce) and formulated a method of resolution and composition using controlled observation.
events.impact: Inspired the Oxford scientific tradition connecting mathematical physics with empirical testing.

events.title: Opus Majus: Scientia Experimentalis & Lenses
events.summary: Synthesized Ibn al-Haytham's optics with European scholarship in Opus Majus, advocating experimental science, quantitative measurement of the rainbow angle (42°), and magnifying lenses.
events.impact: Championed empirical verification as the foundation of natural philosophy in Western Europe.

events.title: Rainbow Refraction Explained with Water-Filled Glass Spheres
events.summary: Used water-filled spherical flasks as single raindrops to demonstrate experimentally that primary rainbows arise from two refractions and one internal reflection, and secondary rainbows from two internal reflections.
events.impact: Solved the geometric optics of the rainbow in parallel with Kamal al-Din al-Farisi, centuries before Descartes.

events.title: Gutenberg Movable-Type Printing Press
events.summary: Combined durable lead-tin-antimony alloy movable type, oil-based ink, and a mechanical screw press to mass-produce accurate books at a fraction of scribal cost.
events.impact: Enabled rapid, reproducible dissemination of scientific diagrams, mathematical tables, and experimental findings across Europe—igniting the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: De Revolutionibus: Heliocentric Solar System
events.summary: Published a comprehensive mathematical model placing the Sun rather than Earth at the center of the planetary system, explaining retrograde planetary loops naturally.
events.impact: Triggered the Copernican Revolution that transformed astronomy and human cosmology.

events.title: Telescopic Observations & Foundations of Kinematics
events.summary: Turned an improved refracting telescope skyward, discovering Jupiter's four largest moons, lunar craters, sunspots, and Venusian phases alongside inclined-plane laws of falling bodies.
events.impact: Overturned Aristotelian cosmology and established inertial relativity and experimental mechanics.

events.title: Astronomia Nova & Laws of Planetary Motion
events.summary: Using Tycho Brahe's precision Mars observations, proved that planets sweep equal areas in equal times along elliptical orbits and later derived the harmonic period-distance law.
events.impact: Provided the exact empirical foundation from which Newton derived inverse-square universal gravitation.

events.title: Descartes' La Géométrie & Analytic Coordinate Systems
events.summary: Published La Géométrie as an appendix to Discourse on the Method, uniting Euclidean geometry with symbolic algebra by representing geometric curves as algebraic equations.
events.impact: Created Cartesian coordinates, making calculus, physics vector spaces, computer graphics, and machine-learning feature spaces possible.

events.title: Robert Hooke's Micrographia & Discovery of Biological Cells
events.summary: Published copperplate illustrations of the microscopic world using a compound microscope, coining the biological term 'cell' after observing the honeycomb compartments of cork.
events.impact: Launched cellular microscopy and opened the hidden microscopic universe later expanded by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's discovery of bacteria.

events.title: Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica
events.summary: Unified terrestrial mechanics and celestial orbits under three laws of motion and universal gravitation (F = G m₁m₂ / r²), supported by fluxional calculus.
events.impact: Defined classical physics and predictive mathematical science for over two centuries.

events.title: Euler's Equations of Fluid Dynamics & Analytical Mechanics
events.summary: Formulated the differential equations of inviscid fluid flow, rigid-body rotation, and variational calculus (Euler-Lagrange equations), recasting Newtonian mechanics in analytical form.
events.impact: Created the mathematical language of continuum mechanics, aerodynamics, and modern field theory.

events.title: Lavoisier's Conservation of Mass & Modern Chemistry
events.summary: Overthrew phlogiston theory in Traité Élémentaire de Chimie, demonstrating oxygen's role in combustion, defining chemical elements, and proving mass is strictly conserved in chemical reactions.
events.impact: Transformed chemistry from qualitative alchemy into a rigorous quantitative physical science.

events.title: Edward Jenner Pioneers Vaccination Against Smallpox
events.summary: Demonstrated experimentally that inoculation with mild cowpox (vaccinia) confers protective immunity against deadly smallpox.
events.impact: Founded modern immunology and led directly to the complete global eradication of smallpox in 1980, saving hundreds of millions of lives.

events.title: Electromagnetic Induction & Field Concept
events.summary: Demonstrated that a changing magnetic flux induces an electric current in a conductor and introduced physical lines of force filling space.
events.impact: Enabled electrical generators, transformers, and the modern field paradigm of fundamental physics.

events.title: Ada Lovelace Publishes the First Computer Algorithm
events.summary: In Note G on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, authored a step-by-step algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers and envisioned general-purpose symbolic machines manipulating music and symbols beyond arithmetic.
events.impact: Articulated the conceptual leap from dedicated calculators to universal programmable software.

events.title: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species
events.summary: Presented overwhelming empirical evidence that all species descend with modification from common ancestors driven by natural selection.
events.impact: Unified all of biology under a single explanatory framework and inspired evolutionary algorithms in modern computer science.

events.title: Maxwell's Equations & Light as an Electromagnetic Wave
events.summary: Published 'A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field', adding displacement current to unify electricity, magnetism, and optics, predicting electromagnetic waves traveling at speed c.
events.impact: Unified optics with electromagnetism, predicted radio waves, and directly prompted special relativity.

events.title: Gregor Mendel's Laws of Discrete Genetic Inheritance
events.summary: Hybridized nearly 28,000 pea plants over eight years to prove heredity operates through discrete paired units ('factors', later called genes) obeying mathematical segregation ratios.
events.impact: Laid the quantitative foundation of classical genetics and the Modern Evolutionary Synthesis.

events.title: Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Table of the Elements
events.summary: Arranged chemical elements by atomic weight and recurring valence properties, boldly leaving gaps to predict the exact atomic weights and densities of undiscovered elements (gallium, scandium, germanium).
events.impact: Provided chemistry's master map and later revealed the quantum-mechanical shell structure of electrons.

events.title: Statistical Entropy & Kinetic Theory of Matter
events.summary: Connected macroscopic thermodynamic entropy to microscopic atomic probability distributions via S = k_B ln W and derived the Boltzmann transport equation.
events.impact: Founded statistical mechanics and provided the probabilistic bridge between atoms and thermodynamics.

events.title: Discovery of X-Rays
events.summary: Detected penetrating invisible radiation from cathode-ray discharge tubes capable of imaging human bone structure, earning the inaugural 1901 Nobel Prize in Physics.
events.impact: Revolutionized medical diagnostics, crystallography, and synchrotron materials science.

events.title: Discovery of Polonium, Radium & Nuclear Radioactivity
events.summary: Coined the term 'radioactivity' and chemically isolated polonium and radium from pitchblende, proving radiation is an intrinsic atomic property rather than a chemical reaction.
events.impact: Opened nuclear physics and earned Marie Curie two Nobel Prizes in Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911).

events.title: Planck's Quantum Hypothesis (E = hν)
events.summary: Resolved the black-body radiation ultraviolet catastrophe by proposing that oscillators emit and absorb electromagnetic energy only in discrete quanta E = hν.
events.impact: Introduced Planck's constant h and inaugurated the quantum revolution.

events.title: Einstein's Annus Mirabilis Papers
events.summary: Published four groundbreaking papers on light quanta (photoelectric effect), Brownian motion (proving atomic reality), special relativity, and mass-energy equivalence (E = mc²).
events.impact: Dismantled absolute space and time while cementing the reality of both photons and atoms.

events.title: Haber-Bosch Catalytic Ammonia Synthesis
events.summary: Converted inert atmospheric nitrogen (N2) and hydrogen under high pressure over metal catalysts into ammonia, scaled industrially at BASF by Carl Bosch.
events.impact: Enabled synthetic nitrogen fertilizers that today sustain nearly half of the global human population, while inspiring modern green electrocatalysis.

events.title: Discovery of the Atomic Nucleus
events.figure: Ernest Rutherford, Hans Geiger & Ernest Marsden
events.summary: Alpha-particle scattering off thin gold foil revealed occasional large-angle deflections, proving atoms consist of a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by empty space.
events.impact: Replaced the plum-pudding model and launched nuclear and atomic quantum physics.

events.title: Alfred Wegener Proposes Continental Drift & Pangaea
events.summary: Synthesized matching coastlines, identical fossil species, and paleoclimate strata across oceans to argue continents slowly drift atop Earth's mantle.
events.impact: Foreshadowed the 1960s plate-tectonics revolution confirmed by seafloor spreading and mid-ocean ridge mapping.

events.title: General Theory of Relativity
events.summary: Presented the Einstein field equations describing gravity as the geometric curvature of four-dimensional spacetime, predicting Mercury's perihelion precession, light bending, black holes, and gravitational waves.
events.impact: Became the foundation of modern cosmology, GPS timekeeping, and relativistic astrophysics.

events.title: Noether's Theorem: Symmetries & Conservation Laws
events.summary: Proved that every differentiable continuous symmetry of a physical system's action corresponds to an exact conservation law (energy, momentum, angular momentum, charge).
events.impact: Serves as the structural backbone of gauge theory, the Standard Model, and general relativity.

events.title: Fifth Solvay Congress: Electrons and Photons
events.figure: Niels Bohr, Albert Einstein, Werner Heisenberg, Erwin Schrödinger, Marie Curie & 24 Others
events.summary: Twenty-nine physicists (17 Nobel laureates) gathered in Brussels to debate the newly forged matrix and wave quantum mechanics, igniting the famous Bohr-Einstein debates on completeness and uncertainty.
events.impact: Crystallized the Copenhagen interpretation and shaped a century of quantum foundations research.

events.title: The Dirac Equation & Prediction of Antimatter
events.summary: Reconciled quantum mechanics with special relativity for the electron, naturally explaining electron spin-1/2, magnetic moment, and predicting the existence of the positron (discovered 1932).
events.impact: Laid the cornerstone for relativistic quantum field theory and antiparticle physics.

events.title: Discovery & Development of Penicillin Antibiotics
events.figure: Alexander Fleming, Howard Florey & Ernst Chain
events.summary: Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mold lysing Staphylococcus bacteria at St Mary's Hospital, later purified into a life-saving drug by Florey, Chain, and Norman Heatley in Oxford.
events.impact: Ushered in the antibiotic era, transforming once-fatal bacterial infections and enabling modern surgery.

events.title: Kurt Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
events.summary: Proved via Gödel numbering that any consistent formal axiomatic system capable of expressing elementary arithmetic contains true statements that cannot be proved within the system, nor can the system prove its own consistency.
events.impact: Shattered Hilbert's formalist dream of total mathematical completeness and directly inspired Turing's undecidability and computability theory.

events.title: Alan Turing Defines the Universal Computing Machine
events.summary: In 'On Computable Numbers', formalized the mathematical concept of an algorithm via an abstract tape machine (Turing machine) and proved the Halting Problem is uncomputable.
events.impact: Created theoretical computer science and proved a single stored-program universal machine can simulate any possible computation.

events.title: Discovery & Theoretical Explanation of Nuclear Fission
events.figure: Lise Meitner, Otto Hahn, Fritz Strassmann & Otto Frisch
events.summary: Hahn and Strassmann chemically detected barium after bombarding uranium with neutrons, while Meitner and Frisch explained the liquid-drop splitting of the nucleus and calculated its ~200 MeV energy release.
events.impact: Unlocked nuclear energy, medical isotopes, and modern nuclear physics.

events.title: Discovery of the DNA Double-Helix Structure
events.figure: Rosalind Franklin, Maurice Wilkins, James Watson & Francis Crick
events.summary: Combining Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling's Photo 51 X-ray diffraction pattern at King's College London with structural model-building at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab revealed DNA's complementary double helix.
events.impact: Immediately explained the physical copying mechanism of heredity and launched the entire field of molecular biology.

events.title: Founding of CERN (European Organization for Nuclear Research)
events.summary: Ratified the CERN Convention on September 29, 1954, creating a peaceful international laboratory for fundamental particle physics on the Franco-Swiss border.
events.impact: Delivered neutral currents, W/Z bosons, the World Wide Web, antihydrogen, and the Higgs boson.

events.title: Bell's Theorem & Experimental Test of Quantum Nonlocality
events.summary: Proved that no local hidden-variable theory can reproduce all statistical predictions of quantum mechanics, turning the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen paradox into a testable inequality.
events.impact: Sparked the Clauser-Aspect-Zeilinger experiments (2022 Nobel) and modern quantum information science.

events.title: Frederick Sanger Invents Chain-Termination DNA Sequencing
events.summary: Developed dideoxy chain-termination chemistry at MRC LMB to read exact nucleotide base sequences (A, C, G, T), earning Sanger his second Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1980).
events.impact: Provided the core reading engine of modern genomics and directly powered the first sequencing of the human genome.

events.title: Discovery of the W and Z Bosons at CERN
events.figure: Carlo Rubbia, Simon van der Meer & UA1/UA2 Collaborations
events.summary: Using stochastic cooling to collide protons and antiprotons at CERN's Super Proton Synchrotron, UA1 and UA2 discovered the massive weak-force gauge bosons right at predicted masses.
events.impact: Provided decisive direct confirmation of electroweak symmetry breaking.

events.title: High-Temperature Cuprate Superconductivity
events.figure: J. Georg Bednorz & K. Alex Müller
events.summary: Discovered superconductivity at 35 K in a lanthanum barium copper oxide ceramic, soon leading to YBCO superconductors above liquid-nitrogen temperature (77 K).
events.impact: Opened strongly correlated electron physics and enabled modern 20-tesla fusion magnets.

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee Invents the World Wide Web at CERN
events.summary: Invented HTTP, HTML, and URLs at CERN so particle physicists across global universities could seamlessly share hyperlinked documents—then released the protocol into the public domain royalty-free in 1993.
events.impact: Transformed global knowledge sharing, commerce, open science, and provided the training substrate for modern AI.

events.title: Grigori Perelman Proves the Poincaré & Geometrization Conjectures
events.summary: Posted three landmark preprints on arXiv mastering Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow with surgery to classify all compact 3-manifolds and resolve Henri Poincaré's 1904 topology conjecture.
events.impact: Solved the first (and thus far only) Clay Millennium Prize Problem, demonstrating the power of open arXiv dissemination.

events.title: Isolation of Two-Dimensional Graphene
events.summary: Exfoliated atomically thin single-layer carbon sheets from graphite, uncovering massless Dirac fermions, anomalous room-temperature quantum Hall effects, and extraordinary tensile strength.
events.impact: Launched the entire field of 2D van der Waals heterostructures and moiré twistronics.

events.title: Discovery of the Higgs Boson (125 GeV)
events.figure: ATLAS & CMS Collaborations (predicted by Englert, Brout, Higgs, Guralnik, Hagen, Kibble)
events.summary: On July 4, 2012, ATLAS and CMS independently announced a 5-sigma spin-0 boson at 125 GeV, confirming the Brout-Englert-Higgs quantum field that gives fundamental particles mass.
events.impact: Completed the particle roster of the Standard Model and opened precision Higgs-sector physics.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 Solves the 50-Year Protein Folding Challenge
events.figure: John Jumper, Demis Hassabis & Google DeepMind
events.summary: Achieved atomic-level accuracy predicting 3D protein structures directly from 1D amino-acid sequences at CASP14, then openly released 200M+ predicted structures with EMBL-EBI.
events.impact: Transformed structural biology overnight and ushered in the AI-for-Science era, winning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

events.title: AlphaFold 3, De Novo Protein Design & the AI Science Nobels
events.figure: Demis Hassabis, John Jumper, David Baker, Geoffrey Hinton & John Hopfield
events.summary: AlphaFold 3 extended atomic diffusion prediction to proteins, DNA, RNA, and small-molecule drugs, while both the 2024 Physics and Chemistry Nobel Prizes recognized foundational neural networks and AI protein science.
events.impact: Cemented artificial intelligence as a core foundational instrument of physics, chemistry, and molecular biology.

events.title: LISA Space Gravitational-Wave Observatory Launch
events.location: Earth-Trailing Heliocentric Orbit (2.5 Million km Arms)
events.summary: Three spacecraft flying in a 2.5-million-kilometer equilateral triangle linked by picometer-precision laser interferometry to listen to millihertz gravitational waves from supermassive black hole mergers.
events.impact: Extends gravitational-wave astronomy across the entire observable universe to cosmic redshift z > 20.

events.title: ITER Research Operations & Burning Plasma Campaign
events.summary: Under the updated 2024 ITER baseline, full magnetic-energy plasma operations begin in the mid-2030s leading into deuterium-tritium burning plasma targeting 500 MW fusion output from 50 MW input (Q = 10).
events.impact: Demonstrates reactor-scale burning-plasma physics, tritium breeding modules, and integrated fusion engineering.

events.title: Einstein Telescope Underground Gravitational-Wave Observatory
events.summary: A proposed third-generation European underground observatory with 10 km cryogenic laser arms buried 200–300 m below ground to slash seismic and thermal noise by an order of magnitude.
events.impact: Will detect hundreds of thousands of binary black hole and neutron star mergers per year back to the dark ages.

events.title: Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee) Precision Higgs Factory
events.summary: Proposed 90.7 km underground tunnel beneath the Geneva basin starting with an electron-positron Higgs, electroweak, and top-quark factory (FCC-ee) in the mid-2040s, paving the way for a 100 TeV proton collider (FCC-hh).
events.impact: Pushes precision measurements of the Higgs self-coupling and searches for new physics far beyond LHC reach.

missions.name: XMM-Newton X-ray Observatory
missions.summary: ESA's high-throughput X-ray spectroscopy flagship with 174 nested gold-coated nickel mirror shells studying hot plasma in galaxy clusters and active galactic nuclei.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Measured relativistic iron K-alpha line broadening near spinning black holes and mapped hot baryonic gas across the cosmic web.

missions.name: Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO)
missions.summary: Positioned 1.5 million km sunward at Lagrange L1 for an uninterrupted view of the Sun's interior acoustic waves, corona, and solar wind.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Mapped the Sun's internal differential rotation and tachocline via helioseismology, monitored coronal mass ejections across nearly three solar cycles, and discovered over 5,000 sungrazing comets.

missions.name: Planck Space Observatory
missions.summary: Cryogenic microwave space telescope cooled to 0.1 K that mapped the entire Cosmic Microwave Background sky in nine frequency bands from 30 to 857 GHz.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Delivered the benchmark measurement of cosmic parameters: 68.5% dark energy, 26.5% dark matter, 4.9% ordinary matter, flat geometry, and tight constraints on primordial inflation.

missions.name: Gaia Astrometry Observatory
missions.summary: Dual-telescope microarcsecond astrometry mission that charted the 3D positions, parallaxes, and velocities of nearly two billion stars in the Milky Way (science observations ended Jan 2025; spacecraft retired Mar 2025; DR4/DR5 releases ongoing).
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Uncovered the ancient Gaia-Enceladus galactic merger, discovered dormant stellar-mass black holes (Gaia BH1–BH3), and tested general-relativistic light deflection across the whole sky.

missions.name: Euclid Dark Universe Telescope
missions.summary: Wide-field 1.2 m optical and near-infrared space telescope mapping weak gravitational lensing and baryon acoustic oscillations across one-third of the extragalactic sky.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Constructing a 3D cosmic map of billions of galaxies out to 10 billion light-years to test whether dark energy is a cosmological constant or modified gravity.

missions.name: LISA (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna)
missions.summary: Three drag-free spacecraft housing free-falling gold-platinum test masses in a 2.5-million-km laser interferometer triangle following Earth's orbit around the Sun.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will detect millihertz gravitational waves from supermassive black hole coalescences, extreme mass-ratio inspirals, Galactic white dwarf binaries, and possible cosmological phase transitions.

missions.name: Solar Orbiter (SolO)
missions.summary: Inclined heliophysics explorer using Venus gravity assists to climb out of the ecliptic plane and capture the first direct images of the Sun's magnetic poles.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Discovered miniature 'campfire' nanoflares heating the corona and directly linked in-situ solar-wind plasma streams back to their magnetic footpoints on the photosphere.

missions.name: BepiColombo
missions.body: Mercury (0.39 AU from Sun; ~0.85 AU avg from Earth)
missions.summary: Dual-orbiter European-Japanese mission (MPO & Mio) entering Mercury orbit in November 2026 to map its huge iron core, active dynamo magnetosphere, and perform precision tests of general relativity.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will measure Mercury's relativistic perihelion advance and Shapiro time delay to test the PPN gravity parameters γ and β while probing solar-wind magnetosphere coupling.

missions.name: JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer)
missions.body: En Route to Jupiter & Ganymede (5.2 AU)
missions.summary: ESA flagship mission arriving at Jupiter in 2031 to perform detailed flybys of Europa and Callisto before entering the first-ever orbit around Ganymede.
missions.physicsDiscoveries: Will characterize Ganymede's unique intrinsic planetary magnetic dipole, measure subsurface liquid-water oceans via magnetic induction and ice-penetrating radar, and study tidal heating physics.

trails.title: From Laser-Vaporized Tin to Frontier AI
trails.tagline: How extreme ultraviolet plasma physics in Europe carves atomic-scale chips in Taiwan that power modern reasoning AI.

stops.title: ASML (EUV Lithography)
stops.bridge: Firing CO2 lasers 50,000 times per second at falling tin droplets creates 13.5 nm ultraviolet light—tested first inside imec's High-NA cleanrooms.

stops.title: imec Leuven (Sub-Nanometer R&D)
stops.bridge: imec defines the pre-competitive sub-2 nm nanosheet and CFET transistor blueprints that foundry giant TSMC scales to billions of chips.

stops.title: TSMC Global R&D Center
stops.bridge: TSMC etches 100-billion-transistor silicon dies and stitches them via CoWoS 3D packaging to manufacture NVIDIA's flagship AI GPUs.

stops.title: NVIDIA Research
stops.bridge: Massive coherent clusters of NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell GPUs supply the petaflops of matrix multiplication that train OpenAI's frontier models.

stops.title: OpenAI
stops.bridge: Scaling transformer pre-training and test-time reasoning raised urgent questions about how neural networks think—spurring former researchers to found Anthropic.

stops.title: Anthropic (Mechanistic Interpretability)
stops.bridge: Closes the loop by peering back inside silicon-hosted transformers with sparse autoencoders to map the hidden circuits of machine cognition.

trails.title: From X-Ray Diffraction to AI-Designed Medicines
trails.tagline: Follow a 70-year chain connecting Cavendish crystal physics, Nobel molecular biology, open databases, and AlphaFold.

stops.title: University of Cambridge (Cavendish Lab)
stops.bridge: Lawrence Bragg's X-ray crystallography physics at the Cavendish spawned a dedicated unit to decode the 3D atomic shapes of hemoglobin and DNA.

stops.title: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
stops.bridge: Decades of X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM breakthroughs at MRC LMB—earning 12 Nobel Prizes—populated the world's experimental protein archives.

stops.title: EMBL-EBI Bioinformatics Hub
stops.bridge: Curated global protein sequences and experimental PDB structures into clean open datasets—giving Google DeepMind the ground truth to crack protein folding.

stops.title: Google DeepMind
stops.bridge: AlphaFold 2 solved the 50-year protein folding grand challenge (2024 Chemistry Nobel), motivating a dedicated sister company to turn predictions into drugs.

stops.title: Isomorphic Labs
stops.bridge: Co-built AlphaFold 3 to model drug-protein-DNA complexes in silico, converging with high-throughput genomic medicine and CRISPR labs.

stops.title: Broad Institute of MIT & Harvard
stops.bridge: Unites AI molecular models with single-cell human genetics and base/prime CRISPR editing to bring programmable medicines to patients.

trails.title: How Particle Physics Accidentally Built Open AI
trails.tagline: Trace the open-science lineage from CERN's Web invention and silica glass fibers to arXiv and Hugging Face.

stops.title: CERN
stops.bridge: To stop particle physicists from losing documentation across global universities, Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 and released it royalty-free.

stops.title: MIT CSAIL
stops.bridge: Berners-Lee moved from Geneva to MIT to found the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), standardizing open protocols carried globally by glass optical fibers.

stops.title: Corning Sullivan Park Research
stops.bridge: Corning's 1970 invention of low-loss fused-silica optical fiber built the transoceanic laser highways enabling instant global scientific preprint sharing.

stops.title: Cornell Bowers CIS & arXiv
stops.bridge: Physicist Paul Ginsparg's arXiv server (stewarded at Cornell) turned instant open preprints into the heartbeat of physics, mathematics, and machine learning.

stops.title: Hugging Face
stops.bridge: Extended arXiv's open-paper culture to open model weights, code, and datasets—empowering labs worldwide to inspect and reproduce frontier AI.

stops.title: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2)
stops.bridge: Completes the open-science stack by publishing Semantic Scholar's literature graph alongside fully open OLMo models, training corpora, and evaluation code.

trails.title: Curved Space, Millennium Problems & Machine Proof
trails.tagline: How pure non-Euclidean geometry shaped General Relativity, solved 3D topology, and entered AI-verified Lean proofs.

stops.title: University of Göttingen
stops.bridge: Bernhard Riemann invented curved n-dimensional manifolds here in 1854—pure mathematics that sat waiting 60 years for Albert Einstein in Zurich.

stops.title: ETH Zurich Mathematics
stops.bridge: ETH mathematician Marcel Grossmann taught his former classmate Einstein Riemannian tensor calculus, unlocking the field equations of General Relativity.

stops.title: Princeton Mathematics & IAS
stops.bridge: Einstein, Gödel, and von Neumann forged Princeton's golden age of spacetime, logic, and topology—directly inspiring France's sister institute IHÉS.

stops.title: IHÉS (Bures-sur-Yvette)
stops.bridge: Modeled on IAS, Grothendieck and 8 Fields Medalists revolutionized algebraic geometry and geometric flows linked to 3-manifold topology.

stops.title: Steklov Mathematical Institute
stops.bridge: At Steklov's St. Petersburg branch, Grigori Perelman mastered Ricci flow to prove the 1904 Poincaré Conjecture—solving the first Millennium Problem.

stops.title: Clay Mathematics Institute
stops.bridge: Steward of the seven Millennium Prize Problems whose complexity now motivates mathematicians to formalize frontier proofs inside software verifiers.

stops.title: Microsoft Research
stops.bridge: Leonardo de Moura created the Lean theorem prover at Microsoft Research, now enabling humans and AI agents to formally verify cutting-edge math line by line.

trails.title: From Abyssal Seafloor Vents to Alien Ocean Worlds
trails.tagline: Discover how mapping Earth's hidden ocean floor transformed our search for extraterrestrial life and cosmic waves.

stops.title: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory
stops.bridge: Marie Tharp and Bruce Heezen drew the first global ocean-floor maps here, exposing the 40,000-mile mid-ocean volcanic ridge that proved plate tectonics.

stops.title: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution
stops.bridge: Diving down to those volcanic ridges in submersible Alvin in 1977, WHOI discovered sunless chemosynthetic life thriving on hydrothermal vents.

stops.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography
stops.bridge: Expanded global ocean-atmosphere sensing via the Keeling Curve and 4,000 autonomous Argo floats—honing remote sensing for icy planetary oceans.

stops.title: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory
stops.bridge: Directly inspired by Earth's hydrothermal vents, JPL engineered Europa Clipper to probe Jupiter's moon for a warm, life-supporting subsurface saltwater ocean.

stops.title: ESA ESTEC
stops.bridge: Europe's technical space hub launched Juice toward Jupiter's icy moons and is now engineering the 2.5-million-km LISA laser interferometer in space.

stops.title: LIGO Observatory
stops.bridge: Proved gravitational-wave interferometry on Earth—paving the way for ESA/NASA's space-borne LISA to hear supermassive black holes collide across cosmic time.

trails.title: From Living Brain Circuits to Agile Humanoid Machines
trails.tagline: Trace the feedback loop from silicon neural probes and biological connectomes to Vision-Language-Action robots.

stops.title: HHMI Janelia Research Campus
stops.bridge: Mapped the complete fruit-fly brain connectome and co-engineered Neuropixels silicon probes (with imec) to record thousands of living neurons at once.

stops.title: Allen Institute for Brain Science
stops.bridge: Scaled open brain mapping to 5,300+ mammalian cell types and cortical connectomes, fueling computational theories of biological learning.

stops.title: Vector Institute (Toronto)
stops.bridge: Geoffrey Hinton turned brain-inspired artificial neural networks and backpropagation into AlexNet (2012), igniting modern deep learning.

stops.title: UC Berkeley BAIR
stops.bridge: Extended deep neural networks from pixels to physical action via deep reinforcement learning and open cross-embodiment robot manipulation datasets.

stops.title: Physical Intelligence (π)
stops.bridge: Co-founded by Berkeley and Stanford roboticists to train generalist Vision-Language-Action policies capable of folding laundry and manipulating tools.

stops.title: Boston Dynamics
stops.bridge: Pairs emerging AI dexterity with decades of dynamic whole-body hardware mastery culminating in the all-electric Atlas humanoid.

stops.title: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab
stops.bridge: Demonstrates how massively parallel GPU reinforcement learning trains rugged legged robots in minutes to hike Alpine mountains and lunar craters.

trails.title: Catalysts, Fusion Magnets & AI Weather Twins for Earth
trails.tagline: How atomic materials discovery, burning-plasma magnets, and AI climate models unite to safeguard a habitable planet.

stops.title: Fritz Haber Institute (Berlin)
stops.bridge: Decoded the atomic surface physics of catalysis and built NOMAD open materials repositories to accelerate zero-carbon chemical reactions.

stops.title: Molecular Foundry & Materials Project (LBNL)
stops.bridge: Published 150,000+ computed crystal structures openly online, powering AI crystal-discovery engines and autonomous robotic synthesis labs.

stops.title: MIT Chemistry & Materials Science
stops.bridge: Advanced high-temperature REBCO superconducting tapes and solid-state batteries—unlocking compact, ultra-high-field magnets for clean fusion.

stops.title: Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS)
stops.bridge: Spun out of MIT to assemble the SPARC compact net-energy tokamak using 20-tesla REBCO magnets aimed at commercial zero-carbon baseload energy.

stops.title: ECMWF (Weather & Climate AI)
stops.bridge: While fusion tackles future emissions, ECMWF's ERA5 reanalysis and AIFS/GraphCast AI models sharpen extreme-weather warnings days further ahead.

stops.title: British Antarctic Survey
stops.bridge: Having discovered the 1985 Ozone Hole, BAS now tracks West Antarctica's Thwaites Glacier to bound future global sea-level rise.

stops.title: Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research
stops.bridge: Synthesizes polar ice, ocean circulation, and energy models into Earth's Planetary Boundaries and climate tipping-point guardrails.

trails.title: Decoding Life: From Heredity to Genomic AI
trails.tagline: Follow DNA from its discovery as genetic code through million-fold sequencing drops, CRISPR, and 40B-parameter genome models.

stops.title: The Rockefeller University
stops.bridge: In 1944, Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty proved here that DNA—not protein—is the molecule carrying genetic heredity.

stops.title: Wellcome Sanger Institute
stops.bridge: Using Frederick Sanger's chain-termination sequencing, decoded one-third of the Human Genome Project and established open global genomic data.

stops.title: Cambridge Dept. of Chemistry
stops.bridge: Just up the road, Balasubramanian and Klenerman invented Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis—slashing whole-genome costs from $100M to under $200.

stops.title: Innovative Genomics Institute (CRISPR)
stops.bridge: Once biology could read genomes cheaply, Jennifer Doudna's CRISPR-Cas9 gave humanity the molecular word processor to edit DNA precisely.

stops.title: Arc Institute (Palo Alto)
stops.bridge: Now trains 40B-parameter genomic foundation models (Evo 2) across 9.3 trillion DNA bases to design novel genetic circuits and Virtual Cells.

stops.title: AHRI & KRISP (Durban)
stops.bridge: Brings high-speed genomics to global public health—tracking emerging viral variants in real time across Africa to protect the entire world.
